body.objective: Students will be able to explore the Spring Festival.
body.iCan: I can explore the Spring Festival.
successCriteria: I can describe Spring Festival traditions in Mandarin and English
I can explain the meaning of common symbols
I can give New Year greetings
body.hook: The Spring Festival, or Chinese New Year, is the most important holiday in Chinese culture, celebrated by over a billion people worldwide and in Chinatowns across Canada. Red decorations, reunion dinners and lucky red envelopes fill the season.

study.title: 春节
study.question: How is the Spring Festival celebrated?
study.passage:
Background (written for this lesson from public sources):
春节 follows the lunar calendar, falling between late January and mid-February. Each year is linked to one of twelve zodiac animals; 2026 is the Year of the Horse.
Traditions: Families travel home for the 年夜饭 reunion dinner on New Year's Eve; in northern China, families often make 饺子 dumplings, shaped like old silver ingots for wealth. Homes are cleaned before the festival to sweep away bad luck. Red decorations (red is lucky) include 春联, poetic couplets hung on doorways, and the character 福 (good fortune), often hung upside down because 倒 dào (upside down) sounds like 到 dào (arrive): "good fortune arrives." Elders give children 红包 red envelopes with money. Fireworks and lion and dragon dances scare away bad luck. The festival ends with the Lantern Festival (元宵节) on the 15th day.
Greetings: 新年快乐! 恭喜发财! (Wishing you prosperity!)
In Canada: large celebrations take place in Chinatowns in Vancouver, Toronto, Calgary and Edmonton, among others.
Activity: make a 红包 or a 福 poster and write two greetings in characters; explain three symbols.

body.objective: Students will be able to explore Mid-Autumn and Dragon Boat festivals.
body.iCan: I can explore Mid-Autumn and Dragon Boat festivals.
successCriteria: I can describe the Mid-Autumn and Dragon Boat festivals
I can retell the legend behind each
I can name their foods and activities in Mandarin
body.hook: Two more major Chinese festivals: under the full autumn moon, families share mooncakes; in early summer, teams race dragon boats to the beat of drums. Each has a famous legend behind it.

study.title: 中秋节和端午节
study.question: How are the Mid-Autumn and Dragon Boat festivals celebrated?
study.passage:
Background (written for this lesson from public sources):
中秋节 Mid-Autumn Festival: the 15th day of the 8th lunar month (September or early October), when the moon is full and bright. The round moon symbolizes 团圆, family togetherness. Families eat 月饼 mooncakes (round pastries often filled with lotus seed paste, red bean paste or salted egg yolk), admire the moon and carry lanterns. Legend: 嫦娥 Cháng'é drank an elixir of immortality and floated to the moon, where she lives with a jade rabbit.
端午节 Dragon Boat Festival: the 5th day of the 5th lunar month (usually June). Teams race long boats with dragon heads, paddling to drumbeats. People eat 粽子, sticky rice wrapped in bamboo leaves. Legend: the poet 屈原 Qū Yuán, a loyal official in ancient times, drowned himself in a river; people raced boats to search for him and threw rice into the water so fish wouldn't eat his body.
In Canada: dragon boat festivals are held in many cities, including Calgary and Edmonton, with community teams.
Activity: groups retell one legend in English with key Mandarin words, then make a comparison chart of the two festivals.

body.objective: Students will be able to compare festivals with my own.
body.iCan: I can compare festivals with my own.
successCriteria: I can compare a Chinese festival with a celebration I know
I can use 都, 也 and 一样 to compare in Mandarin
body.hook: Every culture has celebrations of family, harvest, the new year and remembering the past. Comparing a Chinese festival with one you celebrate shows how people everywhere share similar hopes.

study.title: 比较节日
study.question: How does a Chinese festival compare with one I celebrate?
study.passage:
Comparison language (written for this lesson):
都 dōu (both/all), before the verb: 春节和圣诞节都是家人的节日。(The Spring Festival and Christmas are both family holidays.)
也 yě (also): 中秋节吃月饼, 感恩节也吃特别的菜。(At Mid-Autumn people eat mooncakes; at Thanksgiving people also eat special food.)
一样 / 不一样: 时间不一样。(The dates are different.)
Possible pairs: Spring Festival and New Year's Day, Christmas or Nowruz; Mid-Autumn and Thanksgiving (both harvest and family); Dragon Boat and a summer festival; Lantern Festival and Diwali (both festivals of light); Qingming (tomb-sweeping, remembering ancestors) and Remembrance Day or Día de los Muertos.
Task: choose a Chinese festival and one you know. Venn diagram: date, food, activities, symbols, meaning. Write and present (1–2 minutes) at least five Mandarin sentences using 都, 也, 一样 and 不一样, plus English explanation as needed.
Respect: describe all traditions accurately and respectfully.
